old: Caveat. Two calibration weaknesses remain and are not corrected in the reported numbers. First, the pseudo-observed set is still not MAF-matched; because proper matching lowers the threshold, the reported threshold is the conservative one and matching would admit more outliers, not fewer. Second, the pseudo-observed and observed XtX distributions do not agree well through the body of the range — on the superseded run the audit measured a Kolmogorov–Smirnov D of 0.158 below XtX 8, with the pseudo-observed distribution stochastically larger through the body and markedly shorter in the extreme tail. Distributional overlap is the only model-adequacy check this analysis performs, and it is weaker than §8.1 previously claimed.
new: Caveat. Two calibration weaknesses remain and are not corrected in the reported numbers. First, the pseudo-observed set is still not MAF-matched; on the superseded 3,359-SNP panel proper matching lowered the threshold, which would have admitted more outliers rather than fewer, but that experiment does not establish the direction of the error for the final 3,916-SNP run, whose raw pseudo-observed inputs are not archived. The frequency-matching limitation stands; a guaranteed conservative threshold does not (Section 5.7.4). Second, the pseudo-observed and observed XtX distributions do not agree well through the body of the range — on the superseded run the audit measured a Kolmogorov–Smirnov D of 0.158 below XtX 8, with the pseudo-observed distribution stochastically larger through the body and markedly shorter in the extreme tail. Distributional overlap is the only model-adequacy check this analysis performs, and it is weaker than §8.1 previously claimed.

old: [Observed] The reassurance that is actually earned. Against all of the above, one robustness result stands and should be stated plainly rather than assumed. The corrected re-run enlarged the SNP panel by 16.6 per cent, replaced an uncorrected quantile with an FDR-controlled list, gave TreeMix inferential support for the first time, and corrected the ploidy treatment that inflates FST by up to 31×. The conclusions did not move. Maximum pairwise FST is 0.00232 (SE 0.00053) against 0.0024 before; the ADMIXTURE cross-validation curve is still near-flat, with K = 2 at 0.83925 against K = 1 at 0.84384; and near-panmixia across Ghana's agro-ecological zones still holds. A headline that survives a materially larger panel and a stricter multiplicity correction is better supported than one that was merely never tested. Two limits on that reassurance should be stated with it. It applies to the population-structure results, which the marker-panel rebuilds do not touch; and it is an internal-consistency argument of exactly the kind that the pattern above shows to be insufficient on its own.

old: [Interpreted] Two cautions limit how much any of this can be made to mean. First, the fitted quantity is six off-diagonal between-population covariances, and an unrooted four-taxon tree already uses five branch-length parameters, so m = 0 has one residual degree of freedom and m = 1 has none or fewer. A rise in variance explained from 0.897 to 0.941 between those two models is not by itself evidence of gene flow, and the original manuscript's treatment of the m = 0 to m = 1 improvement as "the one substantive result" applied a degrees-of-freedom argument against m = 3 while exempting m = 1 from it. The edge p-values are the stronger evidence precisely because they do not depend on the variance-explained curve. Second, with four populations, three of which are a single administrative region each, these edges cannot be read as specific geographic gene-flow corridors. What the graph establishes is that a strictly bifurcating tree does not describe these populations, which is what would be expected of a single population with ongoing exchange, and that the selected graph carries two edges whose weights are distinguishable from zero conditional on that graph. Those are conditional edge statistics, not identified directions of historical exchange.
new: [Interpreted] Two cautions limit how much any of this can be made to mean. First, the fitted quantity is six off-diagonal between-population covariances, and an unrooted four-taxon tree already uses five branch-length parameters, so m = 0 has one residual degree of freedom and m = 1 has none or fewer. A rise in variance explained from 0.897 to 0.941 between those two models is not by itself evidence of gene flow, and the original manuscript's treatment of the m = 0 to m = 1 improvement as "the one substantive result" applied a degrees-of-freedom argument against m = 3 while exempting m = 1 from it. The edge p-values are the stronger evidence precisely because they do not depend on the variance-explained curve. Second, with four populations, three of which are a single administrative region each, these edges cannot be read as specific geographic gene-flow corridors. What the graph establishes is narrower than it looks: within this fitted covariance model, a strictly bifurcating topology leaves residual covariance that two admixture edges absorb, and those two edges carry weights distinguishable from zero conditional on that graph. Edge significance is conditional on a fixed topology and root and does not propagate error in the graph structure itself (Pickrell and Pritchard 2012), so this is a statement about model fit rather than a demonstration of ongoing exchange. Those are conditional edge statistics, not identified directions of historical exchange.

old: [Calculated] The four outstanding checks have now been run. Three confirmed robustness; one overturned a conclusion. (i) Threshold sensitivity. scripts/step13_sensitivity.py rebuilds the analysis matrix under six combinations of the two thresholds that define the dataset — the Fws monoclonality cut, which discards 57 per cent of isolates and does so unevenly by zone, and the MAF floor, which discards 99.8 per cent of sites — and recomputes pairwise FST and the region-level Mantel test for each (Table 8.3). Near-panmixia is insensitive to both: maximum pairwise FST moves only between 0.00204 and 0.00255, a total spread of 0.0005, over sample sizes from 1,900 to 4,403 and SNP counts from 3,275 to 10,876. That is the strongest evidence for the headline conclusion in the whole analysis. Isolation by distance is not: the Mantel test is significant in 2 of 6 scenarios, failing at every relaxation of the Fws cut and at MAF ≥ 0.01, and holding only at the published thresholds and marginally at MAF ≥ 0.02. Taken with the leave-one-region-out jackknife, which already showed 4 of 7 and collapse when Upper East is dropped, the finding must now be reported as not robust. It was the manuscript's only positive spatial finding, and it did not survive the two checks the audit itself identified as most needed. That is the overturned conclusion, and it is a loss rather than a refinement. (ii) Outlier variant quality. The 19 XtX outliers are better-supported calls than the rest of the panel, not worse, and the exported-protein artefact worry is closed; two adjacent chromosome-11 SNPs are downgraded for an unrelated and still-unverified reason (§7.2 and its note). (iii) Stage 3 re-run on the 1,900-isolate analysis set. The ordination conclusion is unchanged, the silhouette becomes slightly more negative, and the figures now describe the same sample as every other result (Figure 8.1). (iv) GeoJSON provenance remains open and cannot be closed analytically; it requires a written enquiry to the likely custodian (§9.3). Two secondary observations from (i) are worth recording in their own right: relaxing Fws slightly raises FST (0.00232 to 0.00255), so the polyclonal isolates the filter removes were not masking differentiation; and tripling the SNP count via MAF ≥ 0.01 lowers it (0.00204), as expected if rarer variants are less differentiated between zones.

old: [Calculated] Near-panmixia survives both thresholds that define the dataset, and that is the strongest evidence the analysis holds for anything. scripts/step13_sensitivity.py loads the genotype matrix once, rebuilds the analysis matrix under six threshold scenarios and recomputes pairwise FST and the region-level Mantel test for each. The two thresholds varied are the ones that do the most work in the pipeline: the Fws monoclonality cut, which discards 57 per cent of isolates and does so unevenly by zone, and the MAF floor, which discards 99.8 per cent of sites. Across all six scenarios the maximum pairwise FST ranges only 0.00204 to 0.00255 — a total spread of 0.0005 — over sample sizes from 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and SNP counts from 3,275 to 10,876, and the maximum pair is coastal savanna against Guinea savanna in every one of them. Two secondary readings are worth recording. Relaxing Fws slightly raises FST (0.00232 at Fws >= 0.95, 0.00255 at Fws >= 0.80), so the polyclonal isolates the filter removes were not masking differentiation — the direction a reviewer would most likely suspect is the opposite of the one observed. And tripling the SNP count by lowering the MAF floor to 0.01 lowers it (0.00204), as expected if rarer variants are less differentiated between zones. A conclusion that holds at 1,900 isolates and 3,916 SNPs and also at 4,403 isolates and 10,876 SNPs is being tested rather than assumed.
